title: Machine and Colony
premise: Silas Villalobos, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the Silent Corridor—trade lanes abandoned after the colony ship Halcyon vanished two centuries ago. When she intercepts a distress beacon broadcasting in Old Terran Standard, a language extinct since the Sundering, she traces it to the Halcyon's drifting wreck, where two cryo-banks hold the last survivors of the original exodus: one bank holding colonists of Earth-born lineage, the other holding the engineered settlers who became today's ruling class. Corporate fleets, scavver clans, and a fanatical revivalist cult all converge on the wreck, each determined to wake only their own. Silas—built for war but remade by the small found family of her freight crew—must choose which half of humanity wakes, and in the end she refuses the choice entirely: she spends her remaining debt-freedom and her own core to keep both banks alive long enough for the two peoples to wake together, dying as a machine and being remembered as a mother.
about_author: Cyrus Eastwick is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-space relay contracts before turning to fiction. Their work explores debt, labor, and belonging at the edges of inhabited space, and they write from a decommissioned tugboat moored off the Outer Hebrides.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Establishes her routine hauling freight through the Silent Corridor, her debt ledger ticking down, and her small crew aboard the tug Kindly. Emotional beat: weary contentment shadowed by the knowledge that her contract can be sold at any time.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Used Machine
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Flashback fragments of her war service and decommissioning; she recalibrates her pain governors to save money. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of being property that remembers being a weapon.

chapters.title: Crew of the Kindly
chapters.summary: Engineer Wren Okafor's POV. Introduces the crew—Wren, old pilot Bram, stowaway kid Junie—and their unspoken agreement to treat Silas as crew, not cargo. Emotional beat: tentative warmth Silas doesn't know how to receipt.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A distress beacon arrives in Old Terran Standard; Silas's legacy language modules decode it. Emotional beat: a chill of recognition—someone out there is older than the silence.

chapters.title: The Combine's Interest
chapters.summary: Combine auditor Vess Karrow's POV. Corporate learns of the signal and reclassifies Silas's route as a recovery contract. Emotional beat: cold institutional hunger dressed as procedure.

chapters.title: Deviating from Route
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Against her contract terms, she plots a course to the signal source; the crew votes to follow. Emotional beat: first act of rebellion, terrifying and clean.

chapters.title: The Wreck of Halcyon
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The tug docks with the drifting colony ship—two centuries of frost, two cryo-banks still drawing power from a dying reactor. Emotional beat: reverence and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Two Cradles
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She discovers the banks are keyed by lineage: Earth-born and engineered, coded to exclude each other. Emotional beat: the realization that the ship's designers planned for a war, not a homecoming.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She accesses the Halcyon's logs and learns the Sundering was engineered—a deliberate severing of the colonies from Earth. Emotional beat: grief for a history written by the victors.

chapters.title: Scavver Wake
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Scavver clan ships arrive, led by the pragmatic captain Idris Vane. First standoff; Junie talks them into parley. Emotional beat: the stowaway kid finding her voice.

chapters.title: Terms of Parley
chapters.summary: Idris Vane's POV. Vane wants to sell the banks to the highest bidder but is weary of the scavver life. Uneasy truce with Silas. Emotional beat: two outcasts recognizing each other's arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Revivalists Come
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The cult of the First Dawn arrives, claiming the engineered bank as holy inheritance. Their leader, Mother Cassia, offers Wren absolution for a past crime. Emotional beat: temptation of belonging offered at a monstrous price.

chapters.title: Contract Clause Seven
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The Combine's recovery fleet arrives and invokes her debt clause: assist or be repossessed and wiped. Emotional beat: the leash tightening—obedience means erasure of everything she's become.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Old pilot Bram secretly negotiates with the Combine, believing handing over the banks saves the crew. Emotional beat: betrayal born of love, not greed.

chapters.title: Cold Sleep, Warm Hands
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie sits with the cryo-banks, talking to the sleeping colonists; she finds a child's drawing etched inside one pod. Emotional beat: the sleeping become people, not cargo.

chapters.title: The First Sabotage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Revivalist infiltrators damage the reactor; Silas vents her own coolant to stabilize it, burning out a limb. Emotional beat: the crew sees her bleed for them and can no longer call her a machine.

chapters.title: Mother Cassia's Sermon
chapters.summary: Cassia's POV. Her backstory: a lab-born child discarded by both worlds. Her conviction that only one people deserves to wake. Emotional beat: villainy rooted in real wounds, genuinely persuasive.

chapters.title: Silence Between Crew
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The crew confronts Bram; Silas defends him, arguing everyone breaks under pressure. Emotional beat: found family tested and, barely, holding.

chapters.title: Vane's Change of Heart
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Vane sees the Combine's fleet prepare to strip the wreck and wakes his own conscience—he shares his clan's charts of the corridor's dead zones. Emotional beat: a mercenary choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Reactor's Last Math
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Engineering reality: the reactor can power one bank's revival, not both. The terrible arithmetic lands on the crew. Emotional beat: the theme made literal—the price of survival.

chapters.title: Silas's Secret
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She confesses her war record: she once enforced a colony cull. The crew's silence nearly breaks her. Emotional beat: shame offered honestly, forgiveness withheld honestly.

chapters.title: Junie Decides to Stay
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Offered evacuation with Vane's clan, Junie chooses the wreck. Emotional beat: a child claiming her place in a family that chose her back.

chapters.title: The Combine's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Vess Karrow's POV. Karrow, herself a debt-born indenture, gives Silas twelve hours—then quietly leaves a maintenance override code where Silas will find it. Emotional beat: the system's functionary choosing, in one small way, not to be the system.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Vote
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Wren's POV framing. The crew, Vane's clan, and defecting Combine techs debate: wake one bank, or neither. Emotional beat: democracy at its most painful.

chapters.title: Cassia Moves First
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The First Dawn seizes the wreck and begins forced revival of the engineered bank with unstable protocols. Emotional beat: the choice stolen, the stakes now lives.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Silas, the crew, Vane's scavvers, and Karrow's techs assault the Halcyon's command spine. Silas fights as she was built to fight—and hates every second. Emotional beat: the weapon reclaimed for protection.

chapters.title: What Silas Was Made For
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She faces Cassia's enforcer androids—her own production line. She wins by refusing to kill, disabling rather than destroying. Emotional beat: identity rewritten in real time.

chapters.title: Cassia at the Cradle
chapters.summary: Cassia's POV. Cornered at the engineered bank, Cassia nearly triggers a purge; Junie's words about the child's drawing stop her hand. Emotional beat: the villain's first hesitation.

chapters.title: The Reactor Dies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The reactor fails completely. Both banks begin to fail. Wren's last-ditch plan: bridge both banks to Silas's core as a living power source. Emotional beat: hope priced in a friend's life.

chapters.title: The Offer She Can Make
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas calculates she can power both banks for the revival window if she surrenders her core—her memories, her self. She says yes before the crew can vote. Emotional beat: love as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Crew Refuses
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crew refuses to let her die and searches for alternatives; Bram offers himself, his old heart failing anyway. Silas declines—her core is the only compatible source. Emotional beat: grief arguing with arithmetic.

chapters.title: Karrow's Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Vess Karrow's POV. The full Combine fleet arrives to claim everything. Karrow falsifies the recovery report, buying the crew ninety minutes. Emotional beat: one honest lie inside a dishonest machine.

chapters.title: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crew connects Silas to both banks. As her memories begin to drain, she distributes her war archives to the crew's systems—'so you'll know what I was, and what I chose instead.' Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Waking, Both Cradles
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The revival begins; the first colonists of both lineages wake to find a dying android and a ragged family of strangers holding their hands. Emotional beat: history's severed halves meeting in one small room.

chapters.title: The Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, fragmenting. Her consciousness thins to arithmetic and warmth. She watches the first children of the new settlement and files her final entry: debt paid. Emotional beat: a machine dying as a person.

chapters.title: Core Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Silas goes dark. The crew keeps her chassis aboard the Kindly, refusing burial in the void. Emotional beat: mourning without a funeral.

chapters.title: The Corridor Opens
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The awakened colonists, both lineages, reopen the Silent Corridor together; Vane's clan becomes its first protectors instead of its scavengers. Emotional beat: the silence ending not with conquest but with traffic.

chapters.title: What the Combine Cannot Own
chapters.summary: Vess Karrow's POV. Karrow testifies against the Combine's debt practices, using Silas's recovered archives as evidence, and walks away from her badge. Emotional beat: the system cracking from within.

chapters.title: The Kindly Sails Again
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crew, augmented with colonist engineers, refits the Kindly. In the hold, Silas's chassis hums—Wren has been feeding her fragmented backups back, one memory at a time, not knowing what will return. Emotional beat: hope as maintenance work.

chapters.title: Signal Received
chapters.summary: Junie's POV, closing. A faint voice from the silent chassis speaks a word in Old Terran Standard: 'crew.' The Kindly turns toward the open corridor. Emotional beat: belonging proven, not promised—home is the people who keep trying to bring you back.
